_meta.purpose: Salmon portions. Six regions match the master. These are fishmonger and restaurant trade terms for parts of a side of salmon; no federal or industry cut chart naming them was located, so region naming and descriptions carry NEEDS_SOURCE. The safety layer is fully sourced: 145 F (FSIS, FDA) or opaque and flakes with a fork (FDA). Every temperature below 145 F on any salmon surface is a labelled preference.
_meta.scores_basis: tenderness 5 = most delicate; richness 5 = fattiest (belly). Editorial.
_meta.source_gap: Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute publishes a fillet TRIM guide (trim levels A to E), not a portion map. A seafood industry or university source for collar / loin / belly / tail terminology is still wanted.

regions.name: Collar
regions.short_description: The fatty piece behind the head and gills. Rich, tender, a fishmonger's secret.
regions.long_description: Trade term. High in fat, protected by bone and skin, it takes smoke and direct grilling well and is hard to overcook.

retail_cuts.name: Salmon collar (kama)
retail_cuts.note: Probe the thickest meat away from bone; 145 F or opaque and flaking.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 20 to 30 minutes at 350 F or 45 minutes smoked at 225 F. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Served whole; flake off the bone.
common_mistakes: Throwing it away with the head.

regions.name: Top loin (back)
regions.short_description: The thick back strap above the spine. Leanest, most uniform thickness; the premium grilling portion.
regions.long_description: Trade term. Even thickness makes it the most predictable portion for a thermometer and the easiest to cook to a precise reading.

retail_cuts.name: Loin portion (back strap)
retail_cuts.note: Thermometer through the side to the centre.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 8 to 12 minutes over direct heat; 45 to 60 minutes at 225 F smoked. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Overcooking a lean portion; check early.

regions.name: Center cut
regions.short_description: The middle of the fillet. The best balance of fat and firmness; the all-purpose portion and the classic cedar-plank piece.
regions.long_description: Trade term. Thick and even, with more fat than the loin and less than the belly. Skin-on protects the flesh in smoke and on a plank.

retail_cuts.name: Center-cut fillet portion
retail_cuts.note: The cedar-plank cut. 145 F or opaque and flaking at the thickest point.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 45 to 60 minutes at 225 F smoked; 15 to 20 minutes on a plank at 350 F. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Portion across the fillet; serve skin-side down.
common_mistakes: Skin off in the smoker; it dries and sticks.
Pit too hot; the white albumin pushes out.

regions.name: Belly
regions.short_description: The thin, fat-rich strip along the underside. Buttery; ideal for smoking and grilling; stays moist.
regions.long_description: Trade term. Highest fat content on the fish. Thin, so it cooks fast; the fat keeps it forgiving.

retail_cuts.name: Belly strips
retail_cuts.note: Thin; thermometer through the side, or opaque and flaking.

common_mistakes: Same timing as a thick loin; it is done long before.

regions.name: Tail
regions.short_description: The tapering rear of the fillet. Leaner, firmer, thinner; fast cooks, poaching, baking.
regions.long_description: Trade term. Thin and lean; it overcooks quickly, so it suits fast methods and fold-under baking.

retail_cuts.name: Tail portion
retail_cuts.note: Fold the thin end under for even thickness.

common_mistakes: Smoking a tail portion as long as a center cut.

regions.name: Second cut (tail meat)
regions.short_description: Darker, stronger-flavoured meat toward the tail and along the lateral line. Smoke it, or use it in chowder and cakes.
regions.long_description: Trade term. The dark muscle along the lateral line and near the tail has more flavour and a firmer texture; it stands up to strong smoke and long cooking in a chowder.

retail_cuts.name: Tail meat / trim
retail_cuts.note: Hot-smoked flakes for chowder and salmon cakes.

common_mistakes: Serving it as a centre-of-plate fillet.
